title: Aspherical base change for Grothendieck constructions
statement:
Use the constructions $\operatorname{Th},\operatorname{Gr}$ and nerve of [lem-coef-thomason-grothendieck-comparison], and weak homotopy equivalences of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. A simplicial set is weakly contractible if its map to the one-point simplicial set is a weak homotopy equivalence. For a functor $u:A\to B$ of small categories and $b\in B$, the comma category $(b\downarrow u)$ has objects $(a,b\to u(a))$ and commuting-triangle arrows in $A$; $(u\downarrow b)$ is defined with arrows $u(a)\to b$ instead. Call $u$ left aspherical if every $N(b\downarrow u)$ is weakly contractible, and right aspherical if every $N(u\downarrow b)$ is weakly contractible. Either condition implies that $Nu:NA\to NB$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Moreover, if $u$ is left aspherical and $F:B\to\mathrm{Cat}$ is a diagram of small categories, the canonical functors
$$\operatorname{Th}_A(Fu)\to\operatorname{Th}_B F,\qquad
\operatorname{Gr}_A(Fu)\to\operatorname{Gr}_B F$$
are respectively left aspherical and right aspherical. These functors are the identity on fiber objects and use $u$ on base arrows. A functor $u$ is right aspherical if and only if $u^{\mathrm{op}}$ is left aspherical.

source.place: Zhen Lin Low, Revisiting function complexes and simplicial localisation (2014), Definitions 1.7, Remark 1.8 and Theorems 1.9–1.10, pp. 6–7. No Stacks tag states this homotopical result.

proof.text: For any simplicial map $H:X\times\Delta^1\to Y$, [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-cylinder] supplies the natural homeomorphism $\rho_X:|X\times\Delta^1|\cong|X|\times[0,1]$, including its endpoint formulas. Thus $|H|\rho_X^{-1}$ is a continuous homotopy between the realizations of the endpoint maps. Realizing $H$ is continuous because on each simplex it retains its barycentric coordinates and applies $H$ to its discrete simplex label, so it descends through the defining quotient. This uses the ordinary product topology, without a Kan, finiteness, or nonemptiness hypothesis on $X$.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.8, printed pp. 77–78; cylinder specialization, as stated by the cited node.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence], a natural transformation of functors induces a continuous homotopy of nerve realizations. In particular, if $p:E\to C$ and $s:C\to E$ satisfy $ps=1_C$ and either $sp\Rightarrow1_E$ or $1_E\Rightarrow sp$, its finite-zigzag clause applies: one composite has a single transformation and the other has the empty zigzag. Hence $|Np|,|Ns|$ are inverse up to homotopy and $Np$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. If $C$ has a terminal object $c$, take $p:C\to1$ and $s(*)=c$; the unique arrows $x\to c$ give $1_C\Rightarrow sp$, with naturality from uniqueness. For an initial $c$, the arrows $c\to x$ instead give $sp\Rightarrow1_C$. Thus either endpoint object makes $NC\to\Delta^0$ a weak homotopy equivalence. These are direct specializations of the cited statement, not additional general lemmas.

source.place: Proposition 8.2, following Proofs paragraph (ii), printed p. 29; natural transformations and the finite-zigzag consequence.

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-homotopy-groups-basepoint-change] for free homotopies. It states that continuously homotopic maps induce the same map on path components and homotopy-group maps related by the change-of-basepoint isomorphism along the path traced by each basepoint. Consequently one endpoint is a weak homotopy equivalence if and only if the other is; its last sentence states this explicitly for realized simplicial maps. A homotopy written on $X\times[0,1]$ is put into its $[0,1]\times X$ convention by interchanging the factors. No homotopy here is required to fix a basepoint.

source.place: Section 4.1, printed pp. 340–342 and Exercise 4.1.2; moving-basepoint identity as stated by the cited node.

proof.text: Opposites preserve the homotopy types needed here. Send a realization point represented by $c_0\to\cdots\to c_n$ and $(t_0,\ldots,t_n)$ to the reversed opposite chain $c_n\to\cdots\to c_0$ with coordinates $(t_n,\ldots,t_0)$. Reversal sends deletion/composition at $i$ to deletion/composition at $n-i$, and identity insertion at $i$ to identity insertion at $n-i$ in the reversed chain; on coordinates it sends insertion of a zero, and addition of neighboring coordinates, to the reversed operations. Thus it respects the quotient relations in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The affine coordinate reversals are continuous, and reversing twice is the identity, so this gives a homeomorphism $|NC|\cong|N(C^{\mathrm{op}})|$, natural in functors. In particular weak contractibility and weak equivalence of functor nerves are preserved by opposites. Directly from the commuting-triangle definitions, $(b\downarrow u^{\mathrm{op}})\cong(u\downarrow b)^{\mathrm{op}}$. Consequently $u$ is right aspherical if and only if $u^{\mathrm{op}}$ is left aspherical, proving the last assertion. This is a homeomorphism of realizations, not a claimed simplicial isomorphism of the ordinary nerves.

source.place: Remark 1.8, printed p. 6; coordinate reversal and comma identification written out.

proof.text: We prove the nerve implication for a left aspherical $u$ by a two-sided bisimplicial set. Let $Z_{p,q}$ consist of chains $b_0\to\cdots\to b_q\xrightarrow{\alpha}u(a_0)$ and $a_0\to\cdots\to a_p$. Operators in the $b$ direction delete/compose or repeat $b$-vertices; deleting the last one composes its incoming arrow with $\alpha$. Operators in the $a$ direction do the same on the $a$-chain; deleting $a_0$ replaces $\alpha$ by its composite with $u(a_0\to a_1)$. The two operations commute because they act by pre- and postcomposition on $\alpha$. Thus this is a bisimplicial set, including degrees zero. Forgetting the $b$-chain gives $Z\to C^A$ with $C^A_{p,q}=(NA)_p$ constant in $q$, and forgetting the $a$-chain gives $Z\to C^B$ with $C^B_{p,q}=(NB)_q$ constant in $p$. The nerve convention and the degreewise simplicial constructions are those of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Theorem 1.9, printed p. 6; agent two-sided comma-nerve proof of the stated theorem.

proof.text: For each fixed $a$-chain of length $p$, its fiber in $Z_{p,\bullet}$ is $N(B/u(a_0))$; this category has terminal object $u(a_0)\xrightarrow{1}u(a_0)$. Step 2 contracts each fiber. Thus $Z_{p,\bullet}\to C^A_{p,\bullet}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence: both realizations are disjoint unions over the same discrete set of $a$-chains, each source component is contractible, and all based homotopy groups are computed in that component. For each fixed $b$-chain of length $q$, the fiber in $Z_{\bullet,q}$ is $N(b_q\downarrow u)$, weakly contractible by left asphericity. The realization of this row is the disjoint union of those comma-nerve realizations: no realization relation changes the fixed $b$-chain, so each summand is open and closed by the quotient topology. Each summand is nonempty and path connected, and has trivial based homotopy groups, by left asphericity. Its map to the point labelled by that chain is therefore a weak homotopy equivalence. Taking all chains gives a bijection on components and the same isomorphisms on based groups, proving that $Z_{\bullet,q}\to C^B_{\bullet,q}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, also when the set of chains is empty. Apply [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence], first in one direction and then in the exchanged direction. Both hypotheses are exactly the degreewise weak equivalences just established, with all index sets small. We obtain weak homotopy equivalences $r_A:\operatorname{diag}Z\to NA$ and $r_B:\operatorname{diag}Z\to NB$ given by the two forgetting maps.

source.place: Theorem 1.9, printed p. 6; agent proof using the existing rowwise/columnwise diagonal theorem.

proof.text: The two maps $r_B$ and $(Nu)r_A$ are simplicially homotopic, with the map itself specified as follows. For a diagonal $n$-simplex of $Z$ and $\theta:[n]\to[1]$, the $j$th vertex is $b_j$ if $\theta(j)=0$ and $u(a_j)$ if $\theta(j)=1$. Within either block use its original chain arrows; across the unique transition from $i$ to $i+1$ use the composite $b_i\to b_n\xrightarrow{\alpha}u(a_0)\to u(a_{i+1})$. More generally the cross arrow from any zero vertex $i$ to a later one vertex $j$ is $b_i\to b_n\xrightarrow{\alpha}u(a_0)\to u(a_j)$. Composing consecutive arrows reproduces that formula, so restriction or repetition of vertices agrees with every simultaneous simplicial operator, including those that change the bridge $\alpha$. This defines $\operatorname{diag}Z\times\Delta^1\to NB$, with endpoints $r_B$ and $(Nu)r_A$. Steps 1 and 3 supply the continuous homotopy and its weak-equivalence invariance. Since $r_B$ is a weak equivalence, so is $(Nu)r_A$. Two-out-of-three for the weak equivalences of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], together with the weak equivalence $r_A$, gives that $Nu$ is a weak equivalence. If $u$ is right aspherical, Step 4 makes $u^{\mathrm{op}}$ left aspherical; apply this result and the natural reversal homeomorphisms of Step 4 to obtain the same conclusion for $u$. This proves both nerve implications without invoking either implication as a new node.

source.place: Theorem 1.9 and Remark 1.8, printed p. 6; explicit bridge homotopy and opposite argument.

proof.text: Now let $u$ be left aspherical, $F:B\to\mathrm{Cat}$, and let $v:\operatorname{Th}_A(Fu)\to\operatorname{Th}_B F$ be the canonical functor using the definitions of [lem-coef-thomason-grothendieck-comparison]. Fix $t=(b,z)$ in the target. Write $H=(b\downarrow u)$. An object of $E=(t\downarrow v)$ is $(a,x,\alpha,h)$ where $\alpha:b\to u(a)$ and $h:F(\alpha)z\to x$ in $F(u(a))$. An arrow to $(a',x',\alpha',h')$ is $r:a\to a'$ and $k:F(u(r))x\to x'$ with $u(r)\alpha=\alpha'$ and $kF(u(r))(h)=h'$. Projection gives $p:E\to H$. Define a section $s(a,\alpha)=(a,F(\alpha)z,\alpha,1)$, sending an arrow $r$ of $H$ to $(r,1)$; the identity fiber arrow is well typed because $F(u(r))F(\alpha)z=F(\alpha')z$. Then $ps=1$, and $(1_a,h)$ defines $sp\Rightarrow1_E$: its naturality along $(r,k)$ is exactly the already required equality $kF(u(r))(h)=h'$. Step 2 shows $NE$ is homotopy equivalent on realization to $NH$. Since $NH$ is weakly contractible by the hypothesis on $u$, so is $NE$. As this holds for every $t$, $v$ is left aspherical. The displayed formulas also show explicitly that $v$ fixes fiber objects and sends a base arrow $r$ to $u(r)$.

source.place: Definition 1.5 and Theorem 1.10(ii), printed pp. 5–7; explicit comma projection, section, and natural transformation.

proof.text: For $w:\operatorname{Gr}_A(Fu)\to\operatorname{Gr}_B F$, fix again $t=(b,z)$ and $H=(b\downarrow u)$, using [lem-coef-thomason-grothendieck-comparison]. An object of $E'=(w\downarrow t)$ is $(a,x,\alpha,h)$ with $\alpha:b\to u(a)$ and $h:x\to F(\alpha)z$. Its arrow to $(a',x',\alpha',h')$ consists of $r:a'\to a$ and $k:x\to F(u(r))x'$ with $u(r)\alpha'=\alpha$ and $F(u(r))(h')k=h$. Projection gives $p':E'\to H^{\mathrm{op}}$. Define $s'(a,\alpha)=(a,F(\alpha)z,\alpha,1)$ and send a reversed arrow represented by $r:a'\to a$ to $(r,1)$. The equality $F(u(r))F(\alpha')z=F(\alpha)z$ types this arrow. We have $p's'=1$ and a transformation $1_{E'}\Rightarrow s'p'$ whose component is $(1_a,h)$. On $(r,k)$ its naturality equation is exactly $F(u(r))(h')k=h$. Step 2 gives $|NE'|\simeq|N(H^{\mathrm{op}})|$, and Step 4 identifies the latter with $|NH|$. Left asphericity of $u$ therefore makes every such comma nerve weakly contractible. This proves that $w$ is right aspherical. The definition fixes each fiber object and applies $u$ to the reversed base arrow as asserted. Empty categories cause no extra hypothesis: if $B$ is empty then so is $A$ and every conclusion is vacuous or the identity empty nerve map; otherwise left asphericity ensures each needed $H$ is nonempty, and every transported object used in the sections is supplied by the actual functor $F(\alpha)$.

source.place: Definition 1.5 and Theorem 1.10(ii), printed pp. 5–7; explicit dual comma projection and identity section.

lean.statement: theorem grothendieck_aspherical_base_change {A : Type uA} {B : Type uA} [Category.{vA} A] [Category.{vA} B] (u : A ⥤ B) : (LeftAspherical u → SSet.Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (nerveMap u)) ∧ (RightAspherical u → SSet.Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (nerveMap u)) ∧ (RightAspherical u ↔ LeftAspherical u.op) ∧ (∀ (F : B ⥤ Cat.{t, u}), LeftAspherical u → LeftAspherical (Grothendieck.pre F u) ∧ RightAspherical (SSet.Thomason.grPre u F) ∧ (∀ (a : A) (z : F.obj (u.obj a)), (Grothendieck.pre F u).obj ⟨a, z⟩ = ⟨u.obj a, z⟩) ∧ (∀ {x y : Grothendieck (u ⋙ F)} (f : x ⟶ y), ((Grothendieck.pre F u).map f).base = u.map f.base) ∧ (∀ (a : A) (z : F.obj (u.obj a)), (SSet.Thomason.grPre u F).obj (op ⟨a, op z⟩) = op ⟨u.obj a, op z⟩) ∧ (∀ {x y : SSet.Thomason.Gr A (u ⋙ F)} (f : x ⟶ y), ((SSet.Thomason.grPre u F).map f).unop.base = u.map f.unop.base))
